sections.title: The Meeting Announcement
sections.content:
Michael Kudlick announces a meeting at SRI-ARC about the Network Mail problem discussed at the January 1973 Principal Investigators' Meeting. The meeting was scheduled for February 22, with a second day available if needed.

The goal was to define what a solution should do, what steps were needed, and who should do them. Results were to be published as an RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: The announcement sets a time and place for people to discuss network mail. It aims to turn that discussion into a clear plan.

sections.title: Problems for the Mail System
sections.content:
The RFC notes that several Network subsystems already send and receive mail. The meeting was to consider common user and site identifications, use of FTP for mail distribution, an option to record dialogue for later reference, and a way to handle mail for TIP users.

SRI-ARC was exploring how FTP could deliver NIC Journal mail without requiring users to know NLS.
sections.plainLanguage: Different systems already handled mail, but they needed to work together. The meeting would consider shared identities, delivery, records, and service for TIP users.

sections.title: Possible NIC Services
sections.content:
The meeting would also consider whether the Network Information Center could maintain identification files for users and sites, record selected mail in the NIC Journal, distribute mail through FTP, and provide group identifications for sending to several people.

The RFC asks people who want to attend to contact SRI-ARC.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC might help maintain address information, keep selected messages, and distribute mail. These were topics for discussion, not commitments made by this notice.
